A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ThreadWeaver study. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, wall-clock measurements, training-data statistics, ablations, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and the appendices, alongside additional aggregate speedup calculations.

M1.justification: The fork-join inference procedure, trie-based training, two-stage data pipeline, and mean-centered P-GRPO with clipped acceleration reward remain unchanged. Rewritten pseudocode and condensed explanations do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Polaris training data and evaluation on AIME24, AIME25, AMC23, MATH500, Minerva Math, and OlympiadBench. Hardware-conditioned reasoning and interactive applications in v2 Appendix H are future directions, not evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the sequential RL baseline, Multiverse-zero, Multiverse, all three Parallel-R1 variants, and the same SFT and curriculum comparators. Newly discussed methods such as NPR and PDR are not added to reported experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 Section 5.2 supplements average per-problem speedup with a ratio of mean latencies and a trimmed calculation excluding the highest- and lowest-latency benchmarks. These add aggregation procedures; the retained experiments do not show changed training budgets or testing settings.

E4.justification: The trimmed speedup calculation adds a limited sensitivity check on the influence of extreme-latency benchmarks. Existing ablations, correctness-filtering comparisons, qualitative examples, and repetition analysis remain, although several move into Appendix E.

E5.justification: Table 2 drops the explicit Avg@8 labels for Multiverse and Avg@16 labels for Parallel-R1 variants. Main benchmark rollout counts and eight-run wall-clock averaging remain documented. This is reduced reporting detail, not evidence that run counts changed.

E6.justification: Matched result tables retain their numerical results apart from equivalent rounding. v2 newly reports an aggregate token-latency ratio of 1.14× and a trimmed ratio of 1.20×. Appendix E.3 also introduces an inaccurate numerical summary: both base-model gaps are called roughly 5%, although Table 9 shows gaps of 5.0 and 9.6 percentage points.

T1.justification: The trajectory factorization and advantage-broadcast derivations move from Appendix A to Appendix B without substantive mathematical changes. Shortened notation and the conceptual discussion of Amdahl's law introduce no new proof or formal assumption.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the same three contributions, compatibility with standard inference engines, and comparable accuracy with up to 1.53× token-latency speedup. v2's explicit priority wording restates v1's existing positioning against prior adaptive parallel reasoning.

C2.justification: v1 Appendix D.3 treats base-model performance losses as a limitation requiring existing reasoning and instruction-following capabilities. v2 Appendix E.3 replaces this with claims of capability preservation and scaling, despite unchanged scores and an understated 8B performance gap. v2 also revises the explanation of dataset-dependent acceleration and adds substantive discussion of sequential bottlenecks, hardware constraints, and possible resource mismatches.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and retains most implementation details in Appendix C. However, it omits v1's explicit description of Qwen3-4B filtering of RL prompts and the clarification that the sequential RL baseline receives no preceding SFT. These are documentation changes, not established experimental changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations for NPR, ParaThinker, and Parallel-Distill-Refine, distinguishing their models or orchestration from ThreadWeaver. It also qualifies the discussion of Gemini Deep Think and removes the DeepScaler and Gemini 2.5 technical-report references. The broader positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The main narrative is extensively condensed and rewritten. Preliminaries, detailed inference specifications, several analyses, qualitative examples, and reward-hacking discussion move into reorganized appendices, while future directions become a separate expanded appendix.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column conference layout, redesigns Figures 1–4, rearranges Figure 5 into a horizontal panel sequence, and substantially relocates and reformats tables. Figure 1 loses its duplicate histogram panels, but their results remain elsewhere; the illustrative trajectory is also replaced and coordinated across diagrams.

improvement.justification: v2 improves navigation, adds code-access information, and clarifies speedup aggregation and applicability limits. However, Appendix E.3 replaces an evidence-supported limitation with an overstated interpretation, including the incorrect roughly-5% characterization of a 9.6-point gap, and some reproducibility details disappear. These benefits and substantive reporting regressions leave the net quality direction unclear.
